entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Martim Afonso de Sousa was a Portuguese fidalgo, explorer and colonial administrator who played a significant role in the early modern period of Portuguese history. Born into a noble family, he rose to prominence as a naval officer under King Sebastian I and later became a prominent figure in the establishment of the Portuguese Empire in Africa and Asia. De Sousa's achievements included leading several expeditions along the west coast of Africa and establishing trade relations with various indigenous communities. He also played a key role in the development of the Portuguese navy and was instrumental in the construction of several important fortifications and trading posts. Despite his many accomplishments, de Sousa's life was cut short when he died in 1571 while on a voyage to India. His legacy continued to shape the course of Portuguese history for centuries to come, and he remains an important figure in the study of early modern Portugal.

De Sousa's significance can be understood through several causal antecedents, including his birth into a noble family and his education at the University of Coimbra, where he studied law and navigation. These factors contributed to his development as a skilled naval officer and administrator. Another key factor was the influence of King Sebastian I, who appointed de Sousa as one of his most trusted advisors.
